name: Ürümqi
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Ürümqi: UFLPA supply chain tracing, sanctions and entity list screening, Central Asia trade due diligence.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Ürümqi, scoped from Nashville and screened for US sanctions compliance: supply chain tracing for Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act exposure, entity list and sanctions screening of counterparties, and lawful due diligence on trade routed through Xinjiang's capital toward Central Asia.
intro: Ürümqi is the capital of the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region and its main administrative, commercial and logistics centre. Regional authorities describe plans to make it a regional centre for international trade and logistics and an aviation hub for Central and West Asia. Ürümqi is one of three areas of the China (Xinjiang) Pilot Free Trade Zone, established in November 2023 with Kashgar and Horgos, and hosts an international land port area and an economic and technological development zone. Xinjiang's reported foreign trade reached 435.11 billion yuan in 2024, much of it with Central Asian neighbours, and more than 16,400 China-Europe freight trains passed through the region that year.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Ürümqi mainly because of the legal consequences of Xinjiang links rather than ordinary commercial opportunity. Under the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, US Customs and Border Protection presumes that goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang, or by entities on the UFLPA Entity List, are barred from entry, and importers must show otherwise by clear and convincing evidence. US sanctions and export-control listings also apply to certain Xinjiang-linked entities and officials. Importers, brands, investors and lenders therefore need to know whether suppliers, inputs or counterparties trace back to Ürümqi or the wider region.

matters.title: UFLPA supply chain tracing
matters.text: Desk research mapping suppliers and sub-suppliers to identify whether goods or inputs such as cotton, polysilicon, aluminium, PVC, tomatoes or newly prioritised materials may originate in Xinjiang or with listed entities, giving importers and counsel a sourced picture to inform their compliance decisions and documentation.

matters.title: Entity list and sanctions screening
matters.text: Screening counterparties, their owners and affiliates against the UFLPA Entity List, OFAC and other official lists, and researching corporate links that are not obvious from names alone, such as shared shareholders, addresses or management with Ürümqi-based or Xinjiang-listed companies.

matters.title: Customs detention fact-finding support
matters.text: Lawful factual research supporting counsel preparing responses to US Customs and Border Protection detentions, including corporate histories of suppliers, published ownership information and public reporting, organised so counsel can assess what evidence exists and where documentary gaps remain.

matters.title: Central Asia trade route diligence
matters.text: Background research on traders, logistics firms and intermediaries moving goods between Ürümqi, the Xinjiang free trade zone areas and Central Asian markets, helping clients outside China identify Xinjiang origin, transhipment and possible sanctions or export-control exposure in their trading relationships.

matters.title: Investor and lender exposure reviews
matters.text: Research for investors and lenders outside China on whether portfolio companies or borrowers have subsidiaries, plants, suppliers or joint ventures in Ürümqi or elsewhere in Xinjiang, drawing on published filings, registry data available from outside China and media, with findings presented for counsel's legal assessment.

local_context.title: UFLPA rebuttable presumption
local_context.text: For merchandise imported into the United States on or after 21 June 2022, CBP applies a rebuttable presumption that goods mined, produced or manufactured wholly or in part in Xinjiang, or by entities on the UFLPA Entity List, are made with forced labour and barred from entry. An exception requires full compliance with CBP guidance, complete responses to its requests and clear and convincing evidence that the goods were not made with forced labour.

local_context.title: UFLPA Entity List and priorities
local_context.text: The UFLPA Entity List is maintained by the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force, chaired by DHS, and additions are published in the Federal Register. The August 2025 strategy update brought the list to 144 entities and added caustic soda, copper, jujubes, lithium and steel to high-priority sectors, alongside apparel, cotton, tomatoes, PVC, seafood, silica-based products and aluminium. The list is updated periodically, so it is checked afresh for each engagement.

local_context.title: Sanctions and export controls
local_context.text: Separately from the UFLPA, US sanctions and export-control listings apply to certain Xinjiang-linked entities and officials. A counterparty's presence in Ürümqi does not itself make a transaction prohibited, but ownership by, or dealings with, listed parties may. Lists change, so screening is done against current official sources at the time of each engagement, and legal conclusions are left to sanctions counsel.

local_context.title: Xinjiang Pilot Free Trade Zone
local_context.text: The China (Xinjiang) Pilot Free Trade Zone, inaugurated in November 2023 as the first in China's northwestern border regions, comprises Ürümqi, Kashgar and Horgos areas. Regional figures put free trade zone trade at about 190 billion yuan in 2024, some 44 percent of Xinjiang's total. Trade facilitation measures in the Ürümqi area, including market procurement export channels for small businesses, increase the number of small traders whose goods may enter international supply chains.

local_context.title: PRC legal constraints
local_context.text: Mainland China's personal information, data security and counter-espionage laws make information gathering for foreign clients sensitive throughout the country, and particularly so in Xinjiang. We have not identified any licensing regime for private investigators in mainland China. Research on Ürümqi matters is therefore conducted from outside China using lawfully available sources, and any proposal involving work inside Xinjiang is reviewed with PRC and sanctions counsel.

tdsc_approach: As a US company, TDSC screens every matter touching Ürümqi for sanctions and export-control compliance before work begins, identifying each party, its owners and any connection to the UFLPA Entity List, OFAC listings or other restricted parties. TDSC does not accept engagements that would violate US or other applicable sanctions, does not provide services to blocked persons and does not advise on avoiding sanctions or import restrictions. Work is therefore limited to lawful due diligence, supply chain research and risk advisory for clients outside Xinjiang, conducted from Nashville using official lists, published filings, registry data available from outside China and open sources. TDSC does not undertake covert enquiries, surveillance or purchased records in China, and findings are framed for counsel.

faqs.q: Can you confirm that our supply chain has no Xinjiang inputs?
faqs.a: No investigator can certify that. We can research suppliers and sub-suppliers from public and lawfully available sources, identify links to Xinjiang or listed entities, and document what is known and what remains unverified. Whether the evidence meets CBP's clear and convincing standard is for the importer and its counsel to judge.

faqs.q: Our supplier is in another province but buys from Ürümqi. Does the UFLPA apply?
faqs.a: According to DHS, goods made in other parts of China or other countries can fall under the presumption if they incorporate inputs made wholly or in part in Xinjiang. We can research the supplier's upstream relationships so counsel can assess exposure. The legal conclusion belongs with trade counsel.

faqs.q: Will TDSC send investigators to Ürümqi to audit a factory?
faqs.a: TDSC does not have staff in China and does not undertake covert enquiries there. Information gathering for foreign clients in Xinjiang raises serious legal and practical constraints under PRC law. Any proposal for work inside the region would be reviewed with PRC and sanctions counsel before any decision, and our default is research conducted from outside China.

faqs.q: Can you check whether a company is on the UFLPA Entity List or sanctioned?
faqs.a: Yes. We screen companies, their owners and known affiliates against the UFLPA Entity List, OFAC and other official lists current at the time of the engagement, and research name variants, transliterations and corporate links that simple name matching may miss. We report matches and near matches with their sources.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Ürümqi?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville, Tennessee, and has no office, staff or address in Ürümqi, Xinjiang or elsewhere in China. Engagements touching Ürümqi are scoped and managed from Nashville, screened for sanctions compliance, and limited to lawful research for clients outside Xinjiang, working with the client's trade and sanctions counsel.
